To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the graphical model diagnosis procedures proposed by Mandel and Bradu and Gabriel are extended to two-way tables and that the extension provides a useful tool for data analysts.

(i) the proposed graphical model diagnosis procedures are useful in the sense that they can lead to meaningful response surface models and/or to meaningful two-dimensional Euclidean maps; and (ii) these procedures can be used to detect and correct for model deficiencies.
a response surface model can be obtained for a two-way table by means of a graphical procedure, and that this model can be used for interpolation and smoothing, for Euclidean mapping, and for ANOVA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a graphical model diagnosis procedure which can be applied to two-way tables.
the development of a graphical model diagnosis for two-way tables which can be viewed as an extension of the work of Bradu and Gabriel.
the development of a model diagnosis procedure for two-way tables which is based on the construction of response surface models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the model diagnosis procedure is a useful tool for model building, model checking, model fitting, and model interpretation.
the graphical model diagnosis procedure proposed here is an important tool for the analysis of two-way tables.
the graphical model diagnosis approach is a powerful tool for the interpretation of data in two-way tables and, at the same time, a useful aid in model building.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a general framework for graphical model diagnosis in two–way tables and we illustrate the potential of the framework by means of a number of case studies.
, for two-way tables, a model is a useful tool for diagnosis.
the graphical model diagnosis procedure is a valuable tool in the analysis of two-way tables.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the model diagnosis procedures proposed by Bradu and Mandel are complementary.
, in the presence of a large number of observations, graphical model diagnosis is an effective tool for the analysis of two-way data.

, for the most part, the model diagnosis procedure is successful in identifying the most important sources of variation, as well as the main interactions between them, and in providing a good fit to the data.
